chapters.title: The Apprenticeship of an Empirical Skeptic
chapters.sourcePressure: Lebanon teaches that visible normality can sit beside unreadable fragility, and that later observers make rupture look more legible than it was.
chapters.coreMove: Separate recent calm from earned knowledge before treating any system as understood.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the chapter into a generic reminder that bad things can happen.

chapters.title: Yevgenia's Black Swan
chapters.sourcePressure: Yevgenia Krasnova shows how one improbable success gets rewritten as if the path had been visible before the outcome.
chapters.coreMove: Study a visible winner while keeping the invisible field of failed alternatives in view.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating breakout success as meaningless or as a simple recipe to copy.

chapters.title: The Speculator and the Prostitute
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter contrasts linear paid labor with scalable, asymmetric payoff where many small misses can coexist with one dominating hit.
chapters.coreMove: Judge a strategy by payoff shape, downside, and survivability instead of by hit rate alone.
chapters.commonMisread: Romanticizing every losing streak as visionary optionality.

chapters.title: One Thousand and One Days, or How Not to Be a Sucker
chapters.sourcePressure: The turkey is fed for a thousand days, grows more confident with each confirmation, then meets the reversal on Thanksgiving.
chapters.coreMove: Ask what regime change could reverse the pattern on the very day the pattern feels strongest.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating induction as useless instead of bounded by hidden regime shifts.

chapters.title: Confirmation Shmonfirmation!
chapters.sourcePressure: Beliefs protect themselves by filtering for support, manufacturing confidence that feels like knowledge because hostile evidence never got a fair hearing.
chapters.coreMove: Make disconfirming evidence enter the room before support gets to declare victory.
chapters.commonMisread: Reducing the lesson to be open-minded or look at both sides.

chapters.title: The Narrative Fallacy
chapters.sourcePressure: Story-shaped understanding selects details, assigns causes, removes mess, and makes opacity feel like comprehension after the outcome is visible.
chapters.coreMove: Treat a clean story as an edited object and recover what it cut away.
chapters.commonMisread: Declaring all stories false or useless.

chapters.title: Living in the Antechamber of Hope
chapters.sourcePressure: Improbable upside can become emotionally vivid enough that people overinhabit the lucky branch and neglect denominator reality.
chapters.coreMove: Keep a vivid possible upside in proportion to its actual frequency and cost of waiting.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating hope as bad or ambition as foolish.

chapters.title: Giacomo Casanova's Unfailing Luck: The Problem of Silent Evidence
chapters.sourcePressure: Casanova's visible survival dramatizes silent evidence: vanished failures leave no face, so the survivor gains more instructional authority than the evidence warrants.
chapters.coreMove: Reconstruct the missing denominator before treating a survivor as a teacher.
chapters.commonMisread: Dismissing winners instead of asking what invisible comparison set is absent.

chapters.title: The Ludic Fallacy, or The Uncertainty of the Nerd
chapters.sourcePressure: The ludic fallacy mistakes game-like, bounded uncertainty for the open, adaptive, opaque uncertainty of real domains.
chapters.coreMove: Check whether a formal model's clean boundaries belong to the domain before trusting its precision.
chapters.commonMisread: Saying games or models are useless rather than locally limited.

chapters.title: The Scandal of Prediction
chapters.sourcePressure: Forecasts win authority through formality, numbers, dates, and audience appetite for certainty even when the knowable signal is weak.
chapters.coreMove: Make precision contract when visibility is weak instead of letting prestige expand it.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating all foresight as worthless or refusing to make plans.

chapters.title: How to Look for Bird Poop
chapters.sourcePressure: Under opacity, useful action comes from scouting, probes, traces, experiments, and contact with reality instead of grand long-range prophecy.
chapters.coreMove: Replace far-seeing claims with small exposures that let reality reveal useful traces.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating the chapter as permission for random motion or opportunistic fog manipulation.

chapters.title: Epistemocracy, a Dream
chapters.sourcePressure: Authority deserves less deference when prestige outruns accountability and insulated commentators sell confidence without exposure to consequences.
chapters.coreMove: Grant more trust to people whose claims stay close to feedback, constraint, and consequence.
chapters.commonMisread: Assuming suffering guarantees wisdom or credentials always imply fraud.

chapters.title: Appelles the Painter, or What Do You Do if You Cannot Predict?
chapters.sourcePressure: Once prediction prestige collapses, the practical answer is to build robust, asymmetric positions that survive error and remain open to favorable surprise.
chapters.coreMove: Design the position so being wrong stays survivable and being lucky can still matter.
chapters.commonMisread: Calling every hedge wise or treating robustness as timid safety.

chapters.title: From Mediocristan to Extremistan, and Back
chapters.sourcePressure: Mediocristan has bounded variation where averages behave; Extremistan has scalable, concentrated variation where one observation can dominate totals.
chapters.coreMove: Classify the domain before using averages, intuitions, or protection levels from another domain.
chapters.commonMisread: Repeating the terms without using them to change decisions.

chapters.title: The Bell Curve, That Great Intellectual Fraud
chapters.sourcePressure: The bell curve becomes dangerous when Gaussian confidence is carried from bounded domains into fat-tailed settings where excluded outliers dominate harm.
chapters.coreMove: Deny the bell curve jurisdiction when tail events can dominate the outcome.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the chapter into an anti-math rant instead of a domain-fit warning.

chapters.title: The Aesthetics of Randomness
chapters.sourcePressure: The mind beautifies randomness into patterns, stories, and smooth structures because order feels better than noise.
chapters.coreMove: Distrust the pleasure of a beautiful pattern until it earns contact with reality.
chapters.commonMisread: Treating taste, elegance, or visual order as automatically deceptive.

chapters.title: Locke's Madmen, or Bell Curves in the Wrong Places
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter sharpens the wrong-place warning: respectable methods mislead when the domain does not justify their assumptions, and formality protects the mismatch.
chapters.coreMove: Ask whether the tool has the right address before letting its precision confer authority.
chapters.commonMisread: Thinking the lesson is that formal tools are fake everywhere.

chapters.title: The Uncertainty of the Phony
chapters.sourcePressure: False expertise monetizes prediction theater, Gaussian overreach, misplaced tools, and prestige authority by selling precision the world never granted.
chapters.coreMove: Separate competence that carries its limits from authority that sells finished-sounding certainty under opacity.
chapters.commonMisread: Calling every expert a phony or replacing expertise with instinct.

chapters.title: Half and Half, or How to Get Even with the Black Swan
chapters.sourcePressure: The closing posture is pragmatic: limit downside, preserve optionality, stay open to favorable asymmetry, and stop needing false certainty.
chapters.coreMove: Build a stance that can survive bad surprise and remain available for good surprise.
chapters.commonMisread: Turning the ending into reckless thrill-seeking or passive humility.
